instruction: Populate the spreadsheet with exactly five different AI/ML research papers. Include paper title, arxiv PDF link, and publication date for each.

parameters.window_name: New Large Language Models.xlsx - LibreOffice Calc

metadata.explanation: Task requires exactly 5 papers in the spreadsheet with three pieces of information each: paper title (column A), arxiv PDF link (column B), and publication date (column C). Getter validates all three columns for each row, checking that titles are non-empty, arxiv links contain 'arxiv.org', and publication dates are non-empty. Only rows with all three fields populated count as valid. Expected count is 5 complete rows. Partial credit awarded: 0.2 points per complete row.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly validates all three required fields per row: title (column A), arxiv PDF link (column B), and publication date (column C)
Arxiv link validation implemented with regex pattern matching for 'arxiv.org' (line 21-22, 32 in getter)
Only rows with ALL three fields valid are counted (line 35: title_valid and arxiv_valid and date_valid)
Metric correctly implements partial credit scoring: score = valid_rows / expected_count (line 18 in metric)
Metric correctly handles expected parameter from get_rule (uses expected.get('count', 0), not expected.get('rules'))
Postconfig appropriately saves file with Ctrl+S to ensure data persistence before evaluation
Minor limitation: No duplicate detection for 'different papers' requirement, but this is a minor issue and difficult to implement reliably
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding duplicate title detection to verify papers are 'different' as per instruction
Optional enhancement: Validate that arxiv links are well-formed URLs (currently only checks for 'arxiv.org' substring)
